verses.zh: 約 伯 回 答 說 ：
verses.en: Then Job responded:[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “answered and said.”

verses.zh: 惟 願 我 的 煩 惱 稱 一 稱 ， 我 一 切 的 災 害 放 在 天 平 裡 ；
verses.en: “Oh, if only[NOTE:1] my grief[NOTE:2] could be weighed,[NOTE:3] and my misfortune laid[NOTE:4] on the scales too![NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “answered and said.”
The conjunction לוּ (lu, “if, if only”) introduces the wish—an unrealizable wish—with the Niphal imperfect.

Job pairs כַּעְסִי (kaʿsi, “my grief”) and הַיָּתִי (hayyati, “my misfortune”). The first word, used in Job 4:2, refers to Job’s whole demeanor that he shows his friends—the impatient and vexed expression of his grief. The second word expresses his misfortune, the cause of his grief. Job wants these placed together in the balances so that his friends could see the misfortune is greater than the grief. The word for “misfortune” is a Kethib-Qere reading. The two words have essentially the same meaning; they derive from the verb הָוַה (havah, “to fall”) and so mean a misfortune.
The Qal infinitive absolute is here used to intensify the Niphal imperfect (see GKC 344-45 §113.w). The infinitive absolute intensifies the wish as well as the idea of weighing.
The third person plural verb is used here; it expresses an indefinite subject and is treated as a passive (see GKC 460 §144.g).

notes: Heb “answered and said.”

verses.en: Then I would yet have my comfort,[NOTE:1] then[NOTE:2] I would rejoice,[NOTE:3] in spite of pitiless pain,[NOTE:4] for[NOTE:5] I have not concealed the words[NOTE:6] of the Holy One.[NOTE:7]

Others take 3a as the apodosis of v. 2, and translate it “for now it would be heavier…” (see A. B. Davidson, Job, 43).

verses.en: Is my strength like that of stones?[NOTE:1] Or is my flesh made of bronze?

The word for “misfortune” is a Kethib-Qere reading. The two words have essentially the same meaning; they derive from the verb הָוַה (havah, “to fall”) and so mean a misfortune.
The Qal infinitive absolute is here used to intensify the Niphal imperfect (see GKC 344-45 §113.w). The infinitive absolute intensifies the wish as well as the idea of weighing.

verses.zh: 絕 望 人 的 講 論 既 然 如 風 ， 你 們 還 想 要 駁 正 言 語 麼 ？
verses.en: Do you intend to criticize mere words,and treat[NOTE:1] the words of a despairing man as wind?
notes: Heb “answered and said.”

verses.zh: 你 們 想 為 孤 兒 拈 鬮 ， 以 朋 友 當 貨 物 。
verses.en: Yes, you would gamble[NOTE:1] for the fatherless,and auction off[NOTE:2] your friend.
notes: Heb “answered and said.”
The conjunction לוּ (lu, “if, if only”) introduces the wish—an unrealizable wish—with the Niphal imperfect.

verses.zh: 現 在 請 你 們 看 看 我 ， 我 決 不 當 面 說 謊 。
verses.en: “Now then, be good enough to look[NOTE:1] at me;[NOTE:2] and I will not[NOTE:3] lie to your face!
notes: Heb “answered and said.”
